entries.title: Propositional Atom
entries.statement: The smallest unit of a formula, representing a truth-valued statement.

entries.title: Modus Ponens
entries.refutation: Assign P=True, Q=False to break the implication itself.

entries.title: Affirming the Consequent
entries.refutation: Set P=False, Q=True. Then (P→Q) is True, Q is True, but P is False.

entries.title: Universal Quantifier
entries.statement: ∀x φ(x) means φ holds for all elements in the domain.
entries.refutation: Find a single element 'a' such that ¬φ(a).

entries.title: Empty Domain Paradox
entries.statement: ∀x φ(x) → ∃x φ(x) fails if the domain is empty.
entries.refutation: Define Domain D = ∅. ∀x φ(x) is vacuously true, but ∃x φ(x) is false.

entries.title: Compactness Theorem
entries.statement: A set of sentences has a model iff every finite subset has a model.

entries.title: Group Axioms
entries.statement: A set G with binary op * satisfying: associativity, identity existence, and inverse existence.
entries.refutation: Verify if (a*b)*c = a*(b*c). Check for element e. Check for x⁻¹.

entries.title: Non-Abelian Group (S3)
entries.statement: The symmetric group S3 is the smallest non-commutative group.
entries.refutation: Take permutations σ=(12), τ=(123). στ=(23) but τσ=(13).

entries.title: Integral Domain
entries.statement: A commutative ring with identity and no zero divisors.
entries.refutation: Find a, b ≠ 0 such that ab = 0.

entries.title: Ring with Zero Divisors (Z/6Z)
entries.statement: Z/6Z is a ring but not an integral domain.
entries.refutation: In Z/6Z, 2 * 3 = 6 ≡ 0. Since 2,3 ≠ 0, they are zero divisors.

entries.title: Hausdorff Space (T2)
entries.statement: Any two distinct points have disjoint neighborhoods.
entries.refutation: Find x, y such that every open set containing x intersects every open set containing y.

entries.title: Non-Hausdorff Indiscrete Space
entries.statement: A set with >1 point and indiscrete topology is not Hausdorff.
entries.refutation: Open sets are only ∅ and X. For any x,y, their only neighborhood is X. X ∩ X ≠ ∅.

entries.title: Bipartite Graph
entries.statement: Vertices can be partitioned into two sets U, V such that every edge connects a vertex in U to one in V.

entries.title: Non-Bipartite Odd Cycle
entries.statement: A cycle graph C_n where n is odd is not bipartite.
entries.refutation: In C3 (triangle), trying to 2-color vertices leads to adjacent vertices having the same color.

entries.title: NP (Nondeterministic Polynomial Time)
entries.statement: The set of decision problems solvable by a nondeterministic Turing machine in polynomial time.
entries.refutation: Show that a problem's solution cannot be verified in polynomial time.

entries.title: P vs NP Gap (Conjectured)
entries.statement: NP-complete problems like SAT are not known to be in P.
entries.refutation: A polynomial time algorithm for SAT would prove P=NP.
